key_insight: PG-KINN pairs a KAN trial network with a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, using compact polynomial test functions to improve PDE solving accuracy, stability, and interpretability over standard physics-informed MLP/KAN approaches.
engineering_relevance: The method is directly useful for solid mechanics and constitutive modeling because it handles nonlinear, non-self-adjoint, and inverse PDEs while reducing derivative order and improving conditioning.
method: KAN as the trial solution space with learnable spline activations
Independent compactly supported polynomial test functions in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form
Gauss-Legendre quadrature with integration by parts to form element-wise residuals
evidence_signal: Across benchmarks including crack singularities, stress concentration, Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, inverse identification in heterogeneous media, and complex geometries, the abstract reports consistent gains over MLP and prior KAN-based baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate quadrature and test-space design, so implementation quality may strongly affect conditioning and final accuracy.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
